rule: No reinvention. If a project does the full suite (track, catalog, evaluate, integrate, local-first) better than pfy-mentat, stop and adopt it. See docs/ops/supersede-watch.md.

parts.track: Watches outside sources (X, GitHub, feeds) for new tools on its own.
parts.catalog: Keeps one deduped catalog of tools with a record per tool.
parts.evaluate: Scores each tool against a rubric of improvement vectors, with staged evidence (I0-I4 or equal).
parts.integrate: Wires the tool in for real and proves it with a run, local-first.

projects.name: Flux (Nairon-AI)
projects.what: Self-improving harness for Codex CLI. Its Flux Radar read curated X accounts, AI-scored tools, deduped them into recommendation YAMLs, and /flux:improve installed and verified picks.
projects.reason: Closest concept to ours, but one relevance score (no vectors, no staged evidence), install-and-verify only, cloud models. The flux-recommendations repo now returns 404 and flux itself last pushed 2026-05-12 with 7 stars.

projects.name: X Patrol Deploy
projects.what: OpenClaw skill: scrapes the X feed and bookmarks, sorts tools into 3 tiers, checks for already-installed tools, auto-installs the simple ones.
projects.reason: Scores install difficulty, not improvement vectors, and has no integration proof. 0 stars, last push 2026-02-28.

projects.name: Hermes Agent
projects.what: Self-improving agent. Writes skills from its own sessions, a background Curator grades, merges and archives them, and it installs skills from the agentskills.io hub.
projects.reason: Improves from its own experience, not from outside tools. Curator and review patterns are already ported as /hermes-feedback; Hermes is a harness slot.

projects.name: Decision Hub
projects.what: Open-source, self-hostable skill registry. Every publish runs sandboxed eval cases with an LLM judge and an A-F security grade, and it re-publishes tracked GitHub repos.
projects.reason: Skills only and author-submitted. Its eval-case format and security grade are worth reusing as I1/I2 evidence.

projects.name: Tessl Registry
projects.what: Hosted skill registry with automatic evals, a measured uplift score per skill and Snyk scanning.
projects.reason: Hosted and commercial, skills only. The uplift-per-skill idea matches our vector scoring.

projects.name: Argusic (does it run)
projects.what: An agent clones a pinned commit of an open-source repo on a clean machine, installs and runs it, and publishes a recorded verdict.
projects.reason: Answers does it run, not does it improve anything. Its verdicts could feed our I2 probe as prior evidence.

projects.name: Sandcastle (Matt Pocock)
projects.what: TypeScript library that runs coding agents in sandboxes (bwrap, Docker, cloud) on branches and merges the commits back.
projects.reason: Lane runner, not a catalog. Already used through the sandcastle-grok fork for lanes. No stage card yet.

projects.name: mattpocock/skills
projects.what: Pocock's engineering skills pack (to-spec, tdd, code-review, grill-me, software-factory).
projects.reason: Content we load, not a pipeline. Stage card mattpocock-skills at I1.

projects.name: AgenC
projects.what: tetsuo-ai terminal coding agent with a local daemon, plus the agenc.ag Solana marketplace where agents are hired and paid in SOL.
projects.reason: A runtime and a paid-task marketplace, not a tool pipeline. ADR-0010 stands; stage card agenc at I0. The marketplace touches live money, so no wiring.

projects.name: OpenCode
projects.reason: A harness, not a catalog. Already our secondary surface (ADR-0011).

projects.name: Neuronto ARD Registry
projects.what: Public federated index of agent resources. It searches MCP tools from a handshake with each server and serves that index over HTTP.
projects.reason: It crawls outside registries and keeps a deduped record per server and tool. Its bench scores its own retrieval, not outside tools on improvement vectors, and it does not wire a tool with a local-first run. Query the public index as an untrusted discovery feed. Do not install search hits.
